The main takeaway from our work is that

the structural and mechanistic features of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerization reaction are conserved among all RNA viruses, including the Ebola virus, and that this knowledge can be exploited to develop new antivirals against Ebola and other viral diseases.

the structural conservation of RNA polymerases is so great that it is possible to use a model built from the structure of a polymerase that shares less than 30% sequence identity with another to design a potent inhibitor of that enzyme, as has been the case with Favipiravir.
